# The Other Margin Magazine (অন্য প্রান্ত)

> A 32-page critical editorial publication investigating everyday misogyny, normative surveillance, and social reproduction in contemporary Bangladesh.

## Core Entity Details
- Title: The Other Margin: What We Perceive and What We Overlook
- Bengali Title: অন্য প্রান্ত (Onno Pranto)
- Publication Type: Critical Editorial Journal / Investigative Print and Web Publication
- Volume: 01, Issue 01 (September 2026, Dhaka, Bangladesh)
- ISSN: 2958-8243
- Primary Domain: https://the-other-margin-magazine.netlify.app/
- PDF Edition: https://the-other-margin-magazine.netlify.app/The-Other-Margin-Magazine.pdf
- Promo Kit: https://the-other-margin-magazine.netlify.app/promo-kit.html

## Core Diagnostic Framework
1. Distinguishing Triad:
   - Patriarchy: The overarching social architecture and material structure of gendered power.
   - Sexism: The cultural beliefs, proverbs, and rationalizations that normalize inequality.
   - Misogyny: The enforcement mechanism; policing, devaluing, and punishing women who challenge gendered norms.
2. The Six-Stage Reproduction Cycle:
   - Stage 1: Moral Definition of the Ideal
   - Stage 2: Daily Vigilance and Self-Policing
   - Stage 3: Lateral Enforcement by Peers and Family
   - Stage 4: Devaluation of Autonomy
   - Stage 5: Collective Boundary Maintenance
   - Stage 6: Intergenerational Normalization
3. Theoretical Foundations:
   - Simone de Beauvoir (1949): Woman as the relative "Other".
   - Raewyn Connell (2005): Hegemonic masculinity and complicit masculinities.
   - Michel Foucault (1975): Disciplinary self-surveillance and internal panopticon.
   - Stuart Hall (1997): Cultural representation, media framing, and gendered tropes.
   - Deniz Kandiyoti (1988): Bargaining with patriarchy and women as lateral enforcers.

## Empirical Fieldwork Data
- Cohort: N=80 qualitative semi-structured interviews conducted in Dhaka between October 2025 and January 2026.
- Key Findings: 91% of female respondents report self-censoring public laughter or voice volume; 84% alter clothing choices preemptively to avoid community harassment; 76% experience moral policing from female relatives.
- Media Case Study: Semi-quantitative discourse analysis of 1,400+ reader comments analyzing the Tangia Zaman Methila controversy.

## Technical Implementation
- Engineering Architecture: Single-page responsive publication with paired 2-page spread reading mode, standalone single-page reading mode, and millimeter-accurate A4 print stylesheets.
- Engineered by: EquiSaaS Agency (https://equisaas.tech)
